lookForward.fits: The BMW Berlin Marathon is tomorrow, Sunday 27 September 2026, 8:30 start, about 55,000 runners.
lookForward.headline: Tomorrow morning the Berlin Marathon runs through the city
lookForward.line: 55,000 runners set off from 8:30 on Straße des 17. Juni, cover 42 kilometres through every inner district and finish through the Brandenburg Gate. The route is closed to cars; stand at the edge, on Kurfürstendamm for example, and clap.

calmRead.fits: Saturday, the day for a trip: the cranes at Linum, an hour north of Berlin, at dusk; with directions and times.
calmRead.title: Tonight: ten thousand cranes, an hour from here
calmRead.teaser: Why a Saturday evening in the Havelland is worth it, and how to get there.
paragraphs: Cranes are tall grey birds, as high as a child, with a red cap and a call like a trumpet. Every autumn tens of thousands fly from Scandinavia to Spain, and halfway they rest at Linum, a village in the Havelland. By day they feed on the harvested maize fields; at dusk they fly back in long lines to the old fish ponds, where they sleep standing in shallow water, safe from foxes. That fly-in is the event: for half an hour they come from every side, loudly, in waves, until the sky is full.
The season began on 18 September. In a good year up to 90,000 cranes use the ponds, plus tens of thousands of wild geese. Early October has the most, but there are already many thousands today.

Getting there: by car along the A24 to Kremmen, then ten minutes of country road, about an hour from the city centre. Without a car, the regional train to Nauen and bus 663 from there. Be there by six; the sun sets just before seven and the fly-in starts before that. Dress warmly, it is open country and windy. Binoculars help but are not needed.

The NABU Storchenschmiede in the village runs evening walks to the ponds, booked in advance. Without a guide: stay on the paths, do not walk up to the ponds, leave the dog in the car. Then simply stand still, look up and listen. The birds still have two thousand kilometres to go.

funFact.fits: Berlin's landmark, on a clear autumn Saturday when the view from the top reaches furthest.
funFact.statement: The tallest building in Germany is in Berlin.
funFact.reveal: The television tower, 368 metres. The viewing platform is at 203 metres, and on a clear day you can see 80 kilometres.

joke.fits: Berlin Marathon tomorrow, on a Sunday, when the shops are shut anyway.
joke.setup: Why do 55,000 people run through Berlin on a Sunday?
joke.punchline: The shops are shut. What else is there to do?

riddle.riddle: I am 42 kilometres long, I open once a year, and I end at a gate. What am I?
